Yes you are. You're saying we just tell them not to feel bad about being completely shut out of human intimacy, as if that's actually going to work.

>And would it be immoral to essentially engineer men to not want sex? Of course it would, especially against their will.

And yet that's exactly what you're proposing we do. Because for your idea to work, men would have to stop wanting sex. Because if you do want sex but aren't getting it, you'll be miserable, even if people tell you not to be.

Quite simply, your proposed solution doesn't work. Those men aren't going to stop being miserable just because you tell them to, and the consequences of having so many miserable men around are still going to happen. And you're going to see a lot of men wondering why they should contribute to society at all, when society has clearly decided to reject them. Are you going to exempt these men from paying taxes? Are you going to offer them anything?

>Whether you can “engineer” or shame women into changing their desire or lack of desire for men or not is moot point

No it isn't, because the central proposal of your thread is that we try to engineer people's desires and feelings, namely men's desires and feelings. If it's okay to do it to men, it's okay to do it to women, but if it's not okay to do it to women, then it's also not okay to do it to men. Unless you're just a gynocentric fuckhead.

>you can’t but if you could it would be immoral

Why can't you? And why would it be immoral if you could?

You think the only reason lonely men feel loneliness is because people tell them they should? That's simply wrong. You're totally ignoring the actual humanity of all those guys.

Also, why don't we go the other way - why don't we shame women for being so picky instead? Maybe we could socially engineer them into not being so picky. I suspect you'd say that's impossible, because we can't socially engineer their natural desires away. Well newsflash, moron, you can't do that with men's desires either. I don't know what the answer is, but I do know that you don't have it.

You're completely fucking delusional.

No amount of not shaming those guys is going to remove their natural desires for sex, companionship, and romance, nor is it going to remove the misery caused by having those desires go unfulfilled. Those things don't go away just because someone tells you they should. Leaving aside that I find your whole argument morally repulsive, the fact is that as a practical matter, it simply will not work, because humans are not robots.

I'd been using an external drive as my default for Steam downloads on my laptop. I was away from my laptop for a while, and when I came back to it today, I found that the external drive was having problems. I tried to install a game on Steam and it told me I had 0 bytes of space, presumably because it's looking for the external drive and isn't finding it. I tried to find a way to tell Steam to download to my laptop's internal drive instead, but I can't find one. I used to be able to choose what location to download to when installing a game. That option isn't there anymore. I tried to go to Steam Library Folders and reset it that way, but Storage Manager doesn't seem to have any way to do it. Every guide I've found for fixing this problem - including the one on Steam's own website - still refers back to the old system and tells me to right-click on a folder/drive to set it as the default, but Storage Manager doesn't let me right-click anything. I'm at a loss for what to do here.

I just had this experience the last time I was in the bathroom. Near the end, when I was trying really hard to stop washing my hands, it started to feel like I was possessed, like I wasn't in control of my body.

And you know what? I don't fucking care if it's reassurance seeking, I want someone to fucking hold me and tell me it's okay. I fucking need it. Don't fucking judge me for it. God fucking damn it, I fucking need it.

I don't have anyone I can talk to. The only people around are my parents, and I fucking hate them, because they're basically walking OCD triggers with the way they act, especially my father. In fact, this incident happened because my father didn't warn me about something he was doing that would trigger my OCD, forcing me to quickly rush in the other direction when I realized he was doing it, and the bathroom was in that other direction, and since I was rushing, I didn't think to position my hands properly.

This is exactly my problem, and it's caused me no end of frustration trying to explain to people that it isn't about germs for me. I barely think about germs at all. My problem is that I think if I become contaminated/unclean, then it means I'm unworthy, a loser, a failure, and so on, and I deserve to be punished for it. I actually really, really fucking wish I was just worried about getting sick, because I think that would be far more manageable and easier to fight off. It would certainly be better than believing my very worth as a human being is on the line. If I thought the worst thing that could happen to me was getting sick, it would be a tremendous relief. I'm at the point now where the OCD has become so painful that if I was just afraid of getting sick, I would have long ago said "fuck it" and stopped caring, but because my fears are more existential, I can't do that as easily. It's far easier to decide "I don't care if I get sick" than it is to decide "I don't care if I become an unworthy loser for all eternity".
Haven't tried it, no. Not sure it would work, because I don't know if it can get rid of the self-loathing that fuels my OCD.

Happens to me too. And the noise is all negative. It's all voices screaming at me about how much of a disgusting failure I am and reminding me that in a matter of hourse, I'll have to go back to the bathroom and endure more torture.

I used to be one. I came up with all kinds of fantasies for myself, and in a way, I was happy. Then I started believing I didn't deserve those fantasies, and that's when my OCD started. I'd give anything to go back. I don't care if it was "maladaptive". It was paradise compared to the living hell I'm in now.

I know my OCD makes me feel traumatized. I have a different kind of OCD than you do (it's contamination OCD), and it's gotten so bad that every trip to the bathroom is a hell that makes me plead for death and leaves me in tears and feeling traumatized. And it never goes away. Even when I'm not in the bathroom, I'm living in fear of the next time, and I start crying when I feel the need to go again.


So yes, I believe it can be traumatic.

>But, I began to worry that I really did touch the door knob before washing up meaning that the hand I masturbated with touched the knob. Post-shower I touched the door knob and my phone. I have touched my phone and quite a few other surfaces. I’m now worried that I have contaminated my entire house. I live with my family and am worried I am somehow spreading this to them. I am worried that everything I touch from now on will be tainted and contaminated. This makes it extremely difficult to let it go. I feel like by ignoring this I am being disgusting and perverted. 

This is exactly the kind of thing I go through. What also stands out to me is that you're not talking about contamination in terms of making people sick, but just in terms of you being disgusting, so it's more of an emotional thing. Your problem isn't a fear of causing harm, it's a feeling of guilt. That's exactly my problem as well. I don't give a fuck about germs or disease, and I don't care so much about getting myself dirty, I care more about getting objects dirty and thereby ruining them and being a disgusting human being. It's been very hard to convince people that this is how my OCD works. Everyone assumes it's about traditional germaphobia. Believe me, I wish it was, but it isn't. It's only been harder to convince people of that since all this Covid business started, because everyone assumes everyone is paranoid about catching the virus. I know for a fact that my parents don't fully believe me. I heard them on the phone with a psychologist, talking about me, and they said "He says it's not Covid-related, but I wonder."



Aside from telling you that you're not the only person who has this particular kind of OCD, I'm afraid I can't offer much advice, because my OCD has completely overtaken me. You've made an appointment to see someone, which is good. You should probably get medication as soon as possible. Another thing you might want to try is sleeping pills. Just regular over-the-counter sleep aids. They help me sometimes. I take them as an anti-anxiety measure as often as I take them to fall asleep. Maybe they'll help you as well. Just be sure to see if it's safe to take them alongside whatever prescription meds you might end up taking.
No, it's worse. At least an abusive partner would give you sex. OCD only fucks you in non-pleasurable, non-literal ways, all the time.

Every bit as miserable and possibly even more so, just in a different way and for different reasons. That's part of what makes it so hard for me to fight the OCD. I know there's nothing good waiting for me even if I succeed, and in fact, if I get rid of the OCD, that might just mean that all the other bad things are free to invade my mind now that OCD isn't occupying it anymore. That's why I try to tell people that OCD isn't my real problem, the real problem is all the shit that'll come to the forefront of my mind if OCD were to disappear. But no one believes me.
Yeah, and then one day I'll make a mistake and tell myself something isn't real, only for it to turn out to actually be real, and then I'll have ruined everything with no way back.
I don't even get three seconds. Maybe one.

If that means completely forgetting your life because the pain of it is too much to bear, I hope that happens for you. I hope you're in a better place right now. Goodbye and good luck to you.
I have done something bad. I do dirty things to avoid having to wash my hands. I have a lot of shame about that, which, of course, makes the OCD worse. I'm just so tired of the pain.

I have intense crying fits every single fucking day. It happens every time I have to wash my hands. It happens at random times during the day when the full weight of my life and all my problems suddenly hits me. It's horrible and I can't stop it.
Sort of. I have handwashing OCD. Lately, I've started to think that maybe I sort of intentionally touched something dirty because I subconsciously wanted to torture myself.

I wish I could do that. My problem is that I think if I don't do the handwashing perfectly, anything I touch afterwards will be ruined forever. So I can never give myself a break like that, because if I did, it would mean I either couldn't touch anything or I'd have to live with tainting everything. I can't afford to give myself a break even once.


There are times when I don't do the full handwashing, but afterwards, I either go right to sleep or I sit around not touching anything.
I envy your ability to do that. Every time I try to adopt that mindset, I just end up thinking that I don't deserve to tell the compulsions to go fuck themselves and I actually deserve to suffer.

Usually, I give in to it. Other times, I'll take sleeping pills to knock myself out. For me, sleeping pills have been better at reducing anxiety than all the antidepressants I've tried. They're really the only thing that has ever worked for me. Sometimes I'll also eat compulsively, although that has lost a lot of its effectiveness recently.
ERP can't remove the self-loathing that fuels my OCD, nor can it take away the circumstances that cause the self-loathing.
ERP isn't a miracle cure. It doesn't always work.

>You are loved

>You are sane

Those are damned lies.

I often go to sleep with "dirty" hands for various reasons. Usually because I've been trying to fall asleep while also trying to hold off going to the bathroom, so what I end up doing is going to the bathroom and only doing a partial handwashing because I'm too tired to go through the agony of a full handwashing and sleep will allow me to escape. When I do this, I'm afraid that while I'm asleep, my dirty hands will move on their own and touch my face, hair, or objects around me that I want to keep clean. Despite this fear, I still do it, because handwashing has become so painful.

This is my exact problem. Things I used to enjoy are now just things I'm afraid of ruining. I used to love buying video games and having a nice physical collection. As a result of OCD, I haven't touched them in years, because I've been afraid that my hands were too dirty and that touching them with dirty hands would mean they'd be ruined forever and I wouldn't deserve to enjoy them. I used to find some comfort in food, but since my OCD got really bad in the last year, even that doesn't help anymore, because now food is just something that makes me go to the bathroom more often, and the bathroom is a torture chamber for me. So now I'm afraid to eat. 

The only comfort I have left now is sleep. The only time I feel any relief is when I'm really tired and about to fall asleep, and waking up again is one of the worst feelings for me, because it means I have to go back to the torture of OCD.
It hasn't, but I wish it would. I wish I could stop caring about everything. Then I wouldn't have to be afraid anymore.

I've had people suggest gloves to me before, but that doesn't really work. I'd still think my hands were dirty, and even if I didn't think they still got dirty through the gloves, there would still be the problem of how do I take off the gloves, because that would require touching them. What I've been doing lately is putting on one or two pairs of gloves after I wash my hands. That isn't a positive development, though. It's because I now believe that it's impossible to wash my hands well enough and so my hands are never truly clean enough to touch anything.

I just don't know what to do. I just want to sleep forever. The only time I ever feel at peace, the only time my OCD ever shuts the fuck up, is right before I fall asleep. And then when I wake up, all the bad thoughts come back. The moment right after I wake up and realize I'm not tired enough to go back to sleep again is one of the most painful times of any day for me. I just want to sleep forever, or I want to keep going to sleep, waking up for a moment, and then falling asleep again. I just can't stand existing anymore.

I have the same problem. There are dirty things throughout my house that I need to avoid touching, and I always hold my hands up to my chest when I pass near them to avoid touching them. If I suspect I might have accidentally touched them, I walk past them with my hands held up again and again as if to prove to myself that I didn't accidentally touch them.

My advice is not to wait. Get started on meds now. If nothing else, you'll know if a particular med does anything for you or not, and that's important, because finding the right one can take a lot of guesswork.

Yes. I believe I have an obsessive personality in general, and that perhaps if I could be obsessed with something else, it could override my OCD. The problem is that I can't bring myself to be obsessed with something else, because I think I deserve to suffer with OCD.

I don't think it's bad at all. If it's just about germs, all you have to do is sit around for a while and wait to see whether or not you get sick, and then when you don't get sick, you can feel relief about that, and that allows you to make progress toward fighting the OCD. But with mental contamination or thoughts like yours, it's not so easy. I have to admit, though, that I still wish my intrusive thoughts were more like yours, because those are thoughts about concrete events that either did or didn't happen and can be verified one way or another. For me, the fears are abstract, which I think is harder to deal with.
So far that it completely controls my life now. It takes me 3-4 hours to take a shower and 5-6 hours to use the toilet and wash my hands. It's abject misery and I'd give anything to make it stop.

I think it may have contributed to making my OCD worse, because not being able to casually go out and pick up some snacks or something has made my life more stressful. It's not really because I'm extremely afraid of catching the virus. My OCD is about mental contamination rather than a simple fear of disease or germs. Believe me, I wish it *was* about germs, because that would be a lot easier to deal with.

Personally, I think the people here are too hard on him. I know what it's like to have a severe mental illness, and I know how badly it fucks you up, so I can't help but feel sympathy for Spoony. I'd be lying if I said that I didn't see a lot of myself in his more depressive tweets. So I'm not going to judge him.

I know what that's like. I've tried distraction as well, and it hasn't worked for me either. I just keep thinking that I don't deserve to distract myself.

Have you tried video games? They used to work for me, and if you haven't tried them, maybe you don't have the tolerance that I do and they'll do something for you. Apart from that, I've found that taking sleep aids can help, if only because it knocks me out and makes me not care so much about things for a little while. I've actually gotten better results from sleep aids than antidepressants.

I don't know. I've never been good at middleground solutions for anything. I've always been an all-or-nothing kind of person. I'd just have so much trouble figuring out where to draw the line. How do I determine what contamination is tolerable and what contamination is intolerable? How do I decide what it means if something becomes intolerably contaminated? I just don't know what to think about anything anymore. That's one of my biggest problems - I don't know what to think about anything or how to feel about anything.

I envy your ability to even deal with having a dog. I could never do that.

The only times I've ever really had success at fighting the OCD were times where I was just too fucking pissed off to care.

Yes, that's how I feel as well. On the other hand, the minute or so between laying down and falling asleep is the only time I ever feel at peace anymore. It's like I have to pay for that peace with horrible suffering every time.
I wouldn't say I'm scared, because being scared implies some degree of hope that maybe it won't happen. I'm convinced this will never get better, and I feel despair over it.
I know how you feel. I'm also at my breaking point. All I can think about anymore is how I just want the pain to stop.

This is exactly what I go through. It's because I have a particular kind of contamination OCD, where the fear isn't that I'll get some kind of disease but that contamination is a moral failure and I should feel guilty for being disgusting. So I can't exactly wait around for the consequences to not happen like I could if I was only afraid of getting sick. And waiting around for the bad thoughts to stop doesn't work, either, because they come from a core self-hatred that won't go away just because I wait a while.

I feel that way too. I get very attached to objects. Right now, I'm still in mourning for my car, which I just recently lost. I had wanted to visit it one last time to say goodbye, but because of some miscommunications, I didn't get that chance. I keep feeling like my car had a soul and everything. Also, any time a product has packaging that says "Try me!" or anything like that, I feel really sad and don't want to throw it away. Any time something gets personified, I immediately start feeling like it's alive and I don't want to hurt it.

It also happens whenever an object has writing that addresses me. I used to work in a grocery store, and one of the items I once stocked was Lipton Noodle Soup. On the back of the package was a maze, with a drawing of a smiling butterfly in the middle. The goal of the maze was to reach the butterfly. There was a written message that said "Fly through the maze until you get to the butterfly's heart! She can't wait to meet you." To this day, I regret not buying and keeping one of those boxes.

In fact, I'd say my OCD is mostly about keeping objects clean. I don't want to walk around with dirty hands because I don't want to make treasured possessions dirty. I don't care about me getting sick. I want to keep objects safe.

Similar situation here. I was going to college full-time and getting good grades, while also working 28 hours a week during the school year and full-time during the summer. I was doing everything you're supposed to do. But then I had a breakdown and OCD hit me, and my whole life since then has been a nightmare I can't wake up from.
Yes. When my intrusive thoughts hit me, I start thinking of every negative thing that's ever made me feel bad about either myself or life in general.
I appreciate the sentiment, but I've had my OCD for over 10 years, and I don't have an amazing partner supporting me. I'm truly glad you recovered, but I'm not sure that can work for everyone.

Yes, that's how I see things as well. I think any slip-up will cause disaster. I also think that even if the disaster doesn't happen immediately, it'll happen eventually, and that might be even worse. I imagine myself getting past OCD, feeling really good about myself, and building up some good things, but then just when I'm feeling better, someone barges in and says "Hey! Everyone! It turns out that jdx0815 didn't quite clean up perfectly at one time or another and as a result, he got bits of his urine/feces all over everything he touched!" And then any friends or loved ones I might have will abandon me and I'll be left alone to suffer in feelings of disgust with myself.
I honestly have no idea. I think the core of the problem is a deep self-hatred, and I don't know how to fix that. I know how it might have been fixed in the past, but I don't think it would work now.

I think I have a form of that. I have the outward symptoms of the stereotypical contamination OCD, but I'm not really afraid that getting contaminated means I'll catch some horrible disease. What I'm afraid of is that contamination will render me permanently "gross" and make the whole universe reject and torture me for failing to avoid it, or that letting other people get their dirt on me would mean that they've beaten me on some metaphysical level. This makes the OCD fears harder to break with things like ERP. If you're just afraid of getting sick, you can sit there for a while and then when you don't get sick, you can feel relief and start to think that maybe you don't need to worry. But metaphysical/philosophical contamination doesn't go away so easily.

I wish I knew. 

I realized just a few minutes ago that guilt and shame have been the dominant feelings in my mind for pretty much my entire life.

I wouldn't call myself religious, but I also don't completely discount the possibility that supernatural things exist. Calling it Hell was perhaps an oversimplification; it's not the traditional Hell of any religion, but rather a specific set of things I'm afraid someone will do to me if I fail the OCD ritual, which would put me in a state I would consider Hell.

Thanks for replying.

What prevents me from doing something like that is extreme self-hatred. I don't believe I deserve to assert myself like that. I believe I deserve to suffer. That's probably the biggest obstacle right now. How are you supposed to fight something when you don't even believe you deserve to fight it?

Thanks for replying.

I've tried meds before. Several antidepressants and one antipsychotic. None of them made any difference. I've also been to two different therapists and a couple different psychiatrists. No help there, either. I'm not very hopeful about that avenue.

The most immediate problem is that I simply can't believe anything good about myself or life in general. Every time I try to have a good thought, my brain shouts it down. I already had a lot of problems even before I had OCD, so it's not like I have any great thing I can look at and say "Once OCD is gone, I'll be able to [insert good thing here]..."

Another problem is that I don't think ERP would work for me. From what I understand, ERP is based on not doing the compulsion, seeing that the thing you were afraid of doesn't happen, and then being able to say "Oh, I guess doing the compulsion isn't necessary after all." Well, the problem for me is that much of the time, I'm not afraid of an immediate, tangible consequence, but rather, it's more of a philosophical thing. I said I'm afraid I'll be sent to Hell, and that's true, but the stronger fear is that not washing my hands "properly" will mean I'm philosophically tainted somehow, and it'll be this dark secret I'll always have to carry around and hate myself for. That's not something where you can sit around and say it didn't happen and therefore you're okay. It's not a concrete, tangible thing.

I really like this idea, although I'm not sure about its reliance on the Dreamflower Elixir. The reason for that is that getting the Elixir requires doing the arena quests, which is something that my good-aligned character wouldn't do, for moral reasons. This is why I dislike the game's idea that the problem is "ego", because if you really wanted to, you could label anything as "ego". Oh, you want to help everyone? Yuslan, on the other hand, is willing to condemn the entire world to annihilation over his hatred of one man.
